title: Open Playbook Format (OPF) v0.5
description: Schema for the three-section (Evidence/Posture/Floor) OPF playbook with the verdict-free per-deal precedent record as its evidence shape, plus the digest_version 4 model-facing projection, a hard-rule `manifest`, per-clause critic `dossiers` and a `provenance_index` (issue #228). OPF 0.5 = the 0.4 document plus `opened_with` on every precedent record and `opening_text` recorded for any distinct opening, whatever its origin (issue #233); it replaces 0.4 in place and 0.4 is no longer a supported format. Each distinct non-standard text (a signed text, a non-standard opening, a refused ask) also carries an optional `vs_standard` equivalence label judged once against our standard and blind-checked by an independent model (issue #240). No stance, band, risk or deviation verdict anywhere in evidence or digest. Apart from `vs_standard`, judged verdicts from an opt-in judged run travel only under the vendor namespace `x_judgments`. See docs/OPF-SPEC.md.

aliases.description: Other names this agreement type is known by, e.g. a consuming app's own dial key.

sha256.description: Content address of the template source file (§4 resolution) — a consumer verifies it holds the cited template by hashing its own copy.

composes.description: OPTIONAL — pinned external clause-intelligence modules (OPF-SPEC.md §3.4). Recorded for lineage; wiring into runtime behavior is a later slice.

evidence.description: §3.5 (OPF 0.5) — the verdict-free per-deal precedent record. `clauses` names each clause type with its counts; `precedent` holds one record per (deal, clause type). Every count in `clauses` MUST equal what `precedent` implies (validator-enforced). Advisory at runtime.

posture.description: §3.6 — negotiation intent as generated prose. Soft at runtime. MAY be empty (e.g. a corpus-only compile with no interview yet run).

version.description: Governed version counter (issue #156). Starts at 1 on the first generated Posture; bumped by 1 each time the interview is re-run against an existing Posture. The genesis (compiler-generated) version; a consumer that lets a human edit the Posture owns subsequent versions per §8.

generation.description: Provenance for how system_prompt was produced.

floor.description: §3.7 — deterministic red lines. Hard at runtime. Invariants are OPTIONAL natural-language statements; a judge (not lexical detection) evaluates them. MAY be empty (a corpus-mined playbook compiles with zero invariants).

perspective.description: Whose perspective this playbook is reviewed 'as' — an open-standard OPF instance must say who 'us' is.

party.description: Our legal entity/party name for this agreement type.

counterparty_type.description: What the other side typically is, e.g. 'Educational Institution'.

de_minimis.description: Categories of change accepted even if technically novel. Negotiation knowledge, owned by OPF.

version_files.description: Per-version content addresses (§4, issue #185): sha256 of each SOURCE file's bytes, keyed by the same inferred ordinal citations use — a consumer holding the corpus verifies 'I have the cited document' by hashing its copy. Hashes of confidential files leak nothing; source_uri does and is stripped by the public export profile.

snapshot.description: Corpus snapshot identity (§3.8, issue #185): manifest_hash = sha256 of the canonical JSON of sorted [(document_id, version, sha256), …] — one value naming the exact corpus state this playbook was compiled from.

identity.description: Artifact identity (issue #143) — content-addressed hash + per-section digests, so a consumer can record which exact playbook governed which document and lineage is reconstructible. `content_hash`/`section_digests` are engine-computed and always populated by this compiler; `id`/`version`/`supersedes` are lineage metadata a producer/orchestrator may assign (like `compiler.run_id`) and are omitted, not fabricated, when not supplied. OPTIONAL at the top level (not every producer populates it) — see playbook_engine/canonicalize.py for the canonical-form + hashing definition.

id.description: Producer-assigned playbook identifier. Not derived from content.

version.description: Producer-assigned version label for this playbook id.

supersedes.description: Identifier of the playbook (id/version or content_hash) this one supersedes, if any.

content_hash.description: sha256 over the whole-document canonical form, excluding `identity` and `compiler.generated_at`/`compiler.run_id`.

digest.description: digest_version 4 — the compact model-facing projection of the 0.5 evidence (playbook_engine/digest.py build_digest_v4): per clause our standard, the deals that opened with it and kept it, the positions of the signed texts, the non-standard signed variants (with how many deals conceded each from our standard and how many signed it as proposed; the variants judged `equivalent` collapse into one entry), the refused asks and the openings not signed as proposed, plus the clause types with no evidence. Optional in the schema; the reference engine always emits it, and when present it MUST equal build_digest_v4(document) (validator-enforced). No `full_text` anywhere; no stance, band, risk or deviation fields; the only judged value is the `vs_standard` label, an index and never an instruction. Covered by identity.content_hash like every content section.

perspective.description: Copy of the document's top-level `perspective` (null when absent) — the digest always says who 'us' is.

n_signed.description: In-scope deals with a detected executed copy.

uncovered_clause_types.description: Every classifier-eligible taxonomy entry (status `active` or `custom`) with no `evidence.clauses[]` entry, sorted by taxonomy_id and never capped: a recognised clause type with no precedent in this corpus, nothing more.

manifest.description: The hard-rule manifest (OPF 0.5, issue #228): one rule per `floor.invariants[]` entry whose deletion or absence is a hard rejection, so a consumer can enforce hard-rejection recall outside both models. Derived only from the signed Floor (never from precedent counts) and MUST equal build_manifest(document) (validator-enforced). No judged verdict. Covered by identity.content_hash. Optional in the schema; the reference engine always emits it (about 2,000 tokens on a real Floor).

dossiers.description: Critic dossiers (OPF 0.5, issue #228): one bounded dossier per `evidence.clauses[]` entry, keyed by clause id, each with at most two precedent excerpts chosen by a fixed order and a budget of `max(1000, 3 * tokens(our_standard.text))` tokens (canonical JSON chars / 4); over budget, whole parts are dropped (never cut): listed Floor rules, last first, while the dossier holding only its first excerpt is still over budget, then excerpts in reverse selection order, keeping the first, until it fits. A dossier always keeps one complete excerpt (when the clause has any), even if that alone puts it over budget: that is the only case where a dossier may exceed its budget. Adding precedents changes which excerpts appear, never adds to a dossier (a dossier carries no count). MUST equal build_dossiers(document) (validator-enforced). Covered by identity.content_hash. Optional in the schema; the reference engine always emits it.

provenance_index.description: Where every dossier excerpt came from, kept or dropped for size (OPF 0.5, issue #228). Not sent to a model. `dossiers` maps a clause id to each excerpt the dossier selected, in selection order: the kept excerpts (`omitted` false), then the ones dropped whole to fit the budget (`omitted` true), so every `omitted_precedent_ids` entry resolves here to its deal; `documents` lists every deal behind those rows. MUST equal build_provenance_index(document) (validator-enforced). Covered by identity.content_hash.

documents.description: One entry per deal a selected excerpt was taken from, kept or omitted, sorted by `document_id`.

omitted.description: true when the dossier dropped this excerpt whole to fit its budget (it is then named in the dossier's `omitted_precedent_ids`); false when the dossier lists it.

signedAt.description: An ISO-8601 date, or the YYYY-Qn quarter `playbook publish` coarsens it to.

vs_standard.description: The equivalence label of this text against our standard, judged once per distinct text (OPF 0.5, issue #240); null = not yet judged (never guessed), and always null for a text whose `standard` fact is true and for a clause with no `our_standard`. An index the consuming model checks against the cited text, never an instruction.

precedentClause.description: One clause type (OPF 0.5). The n_* counts are derived from evidence.precedent and MUST equal what it implies.

n_deals.description: Distinct deals with a precedent record for this clause.

n_signed_standard.description: Distinct signed deals whose signed text is our standard language (`standard: true`).

n_variants.description: Distinct non-standard texts signed in signed deals, grouped by normalized text (exact after normalization).

n_refused.description: Distinct refused-ask texts, grouped the same way.

n_opened_standard.description: Distinct signed deals whose clause opened with our standard (`opened_with` is `standard`).

n_kept_standard.description: Of those deals, the ones whose signed text is our standard language (`standard: true`).

n_changed_openings.description: Distinct non-standard openings that were not signed as proposed (a signed deal's `opened_with` is `non_standard` and `opening_text` is set), grouped by the §3.5.4 grouping key, excluding an opening that is also one of the same deal's refused asks. Equals the digest's `n_changed_openings_total`.

refusedAsk.description: Text proposed during the negotiation and struck before signing.

round.description: Round the ask arrived in: the cited draft's version ordinal - 1 (0 = the opening draft).

vs_standard.description: The equivalence label of this text against our standard, judged once per distinct text (OPF 0.5, issue #240); null = not yet judged (never guessed), and always null for a text whose `standard` fact is true and for a clause with no `our_standard`. An index the consuming model checks against the cited text, never an instruction.

precedent.description: One deal's record for one clause type (OPF 0.5) — facts only, never a judged verdict. At most one record per (document_id, taxonomy_id).

id.description: "prec." + the first 16 hex chars of sha256(canonical([agreement_type.id, document_id, taxonomy_id, signed_text.text or ""])).

paper.description: Whose paper the deal is on — metadata only; never partitions, gates or weights anything.

signed.description: The deal has a detected executed copy; MUST agree with corpus.documents[].signed_version.

rounds.description: Distinct negotiation rounds in which this clause changed.

signed_text.description: The deal's terminal text for the clause (the executed copy when `signed`, else the last draft); null when the clause was struck before signing.

opened_with.description: What the clause opened with, a fact about the deal's first draft (the first version in negotiation order; the signed copy itself for a single-version deal), whatever its origin and whatever paper the deal is on. `standard`: the first-draft text of the clause type is our standard language (the same exact check `standard` uses). `non_standard`: present but not standard, including a clause type with no template clause. `absent`: the first draft has no node of the clause type (it was added during negotiation). null: not determined, i.e. the deal has no detected executed copy (`signed` false) or the store predates this field. MUST be null when `signed` is false. Never a judged verdict.

opening_text.description: The first-draft text of the clause type (every first-draft node bound into an aligned row of it, joined with a newline in first-draft order; `ref` cites the first node), whatever its origin. Recorded when `opened_with` is `standard` or `non_standard` AND either `signed_text` is null or the §3.5.4 grouping key of the opening differs from that of `signed_text`; null otherwise. null means "not recorded / not distinct", never "opened with the signed text" when `opened_with` is null. When non-null, `moved` MUST be true.

standard.description: signed_text is our standard language: an exact match after normalization (deterministic, never judged). False when signed_text is null.

moved.description: The clause changed during the negotiation, was struck, or carried a refused ask. Always true when `opening_text` is non-null.

digestVariant.description: One non-standard text signed in at least one deal (one §3.5.4 grouping key).

text.description: Sentence-boundary summary (≤ 300 chars) of the group's representative signed text.

n_from_standard.description: Deals in the group whose clause opened with our standard: the variant is a concession on record.

n_unchanged.description: Deals in the group whose clause opened non-standard and was signed exactly as it opened (`opening_text` null).

label.description: The `vs_standard.label` of the group's representative text (OPF-SPEC §3.5.6), or null when it is not judged. An index the consuming model checks against the cited text, never an instruction.
The `vs_standard.label` of the group's representative text (OPF-SPEC §3.5.6), or null when it is not judged. An index the consuming model checks against the cited text, never an instruction.

n_opened_standard.description: Distinct signed deals whose clause opened with our standard.

n_kept_standard.description: Of those, deals whose signed text is our standard language.

signed_variants.description: Signed variants: `less_protective` and `different_concept` first, then unjudged, then `more_protective`, each tier ordered n_deals desc, last_signed desc, then normalized text; the single collapsed `equivalent` entry last. The cap applies after collapsing (see n_variants_total).

refused_asks.description: Refused asks, ordered n_deals desc, then normalized text; capped (see n_refused_total).

changed_openings.description: Non-standard openings not signed as proposed, ordered n_deals desc, then normalized text; capped (see n_changed_openings_total).

n_changed_openings_total.description: Uncapped number of changed openings; equals evidence.clauses[].n_changed_openings.

xJudgment.description: One judged verdict from an opt-in judged run, keyed by precedent id. Vendor-namespace data: never part of evidence.precedent or the digest.

vsStandardVerdict.description: A drafted, blind-checked equivalence verdict for one distinct text, relative to `perspective.party`.

label.description: `equivalent`: the same legal effect for perspective.party as our standard. `more_protective`: better for perspective.party than our standard. `less_protective`: worse for perspective.party. `different_concept`: it does something our standard does not (or omits what it does), so protectiveness cannot be compared.

reason.description: One sentence naming the operative difference. No deal or counterparty names.

basis.description: Who produced the verdict: the store-backed judge, an agent acting as the judge, or an owner correction (which wins over any agent or check answer).

by.description: The model id of the independent checker (or, when `adjudicated`, of the adjudicator).

adjudicated.description: True when the check disagreed and a fresh agent's answer was stored as the verdict; false with `agreed: false` means the disagreement awaits adjudication.

check.description: The independent blind check of this verdict; null = not checked yet.

digestEquivalentVariants.description: All signed variants labelled `equivalent` to our standard, collapsed into ONE entry.

n_deals.description: Distinct deals that signed any of the collapsed texts.

n_texts.description: How many distinct texts (§3.5.4 grouping keys) collapsed into this entry.

exemplars.description: At most two of the collapsed texts, in group order (n_deals desc, last_signed desc, then normalized text).

digestChangedOpening.description: Non-standard opening language that was not signed as proposed (one §3.5.4 grouping key of `opening_text`).

text.description: Sentence-boundary summary (≤ 300 chars) of the representative (lowest document_id) opening.

n_to_standard.description: Deals in the group whose signed text is our standard language.

n_struck.description: Deals in the group whose clause was struck (`signed_text` null).

label.description: The `vs_standard.label` of the group's representative text (OPF-SPEC §3.5.6), or null when it is not judged. An index the consuming model checks against the cited text, never an instruction.

digestPositions.description: Distinct signed deals that signed a text for the clause, by position: our standard, each `vs_standard` label of a non-standard text, or unjudged.

hardRuleCondition.description: A deterministic predicate spec the consumer can evaluate outside any model, or the string "judged" for a rule that is not machine-evaluable. `required_phrases`: the clause text contains every (`match` all, the default) or any phrase, compared case-insensitively on normalized whitespace. `numeric_bound`: the number `pattern` (a regex with exactly one capture group) captures is at least `min` and at most `max`. `cross_reference`: the clause text cross-references the clause `clause_id`. The validator enforces the finer rules (regex compiles with one group, at least one bound, non-blank phrases).

hardRule.description: One hard rule (OPF 0.5, issue #228), derived from one `floor.invariants[]` entry and never from precedent counts. `clause_id` / `taxonomy_id` come from the invariant's `x_taxonomy_id` (null when it names none or the corpus has no evidence for it); `required_presence`, `condition` and `permissible_proof` from its `x_required_presence`, `x_condition` and `x_permissible_proof` (defaults: false, "judged", []); `fallback_language` is the clause's `our_standard.text` (null when there is none). A rule that demands presence (`required_presence` true) or carries a predicate (`condition` other than "judged") MUST name its clause: `taxonomy_id` is then a string, because a predicate is checked against the text of the clause it names and a presence rule rejects that clause's absence (OPF-SPEC §3.12.3).

required_presence.description: The clause's absence or deletion is a hard rejection.

dossierExcerpt.description: One precedent record as an opening-to-signed pair, verbatim and WHOLE: the record's own text, never a prefix or an ellipsis cut (a dossier over its budget drops whole excerpts instead, naming them in `omitted_precedent_ids`). `opening` is the record's `opening_text` (null when none is recorded: the excerpt is the signed text alone); `signed` its `signed_text` (null when struck before signing). A `refused_ask` excerpt carries the ask as `opening` and what the deal signed instead as `signed`.

kind.description: Which digest list the excerpt's group came from.

dossier.description: A bounded critic dossier for one clause (OPF 0.5, issue #228): at most two excerpts, every text WHOLE (nothing is cut part-way: a cut-off clause can drop its operative carve-out or cap and so plant a false fact). Its budget is `max(1000, 3 * tokens(our_standard.text))` tokens (canonical JSON chars / 4; 1,000 when there is no our standard); over budget, WHOLE parts are dropped: the listed Floor rules, last first, while the dossier holding only its first excerpt (none, when the clause has none) is still over budget, then excerpts in reverse selection order, keeping the first, until it fits. Our standard and the identifiers are never dropped. A dossier keeps at least one complete excerpt (when the clause has any), even if that one alone puts it over budget: a dossier holding its single kept excerpt is the only one that may exceed its budget, and a dossier with no excerpt over its budget is invalid. Facts only: our standard, the signed Floor's own statements and rationale for the clause, and the selected excerpts. `n_floor_rules` is the uncapped number of Floor rules for the clause (at most three are listed, fewer when rules are dropped for size; the manifest states every one).

n_omitted.description: How many selected excerpts were dropped whole to fit the budget; always equals the length of `omitted_precedent_ids`.

omitted_precedent_ids.description: The `precedent_id` of each dropped excerpt, sorted; each resolves to its deal through `provenance_index.dossiers` (a row with `omitted` true) and to its record in `evidence.precedent` (OPF-SPEC §3.12.3).
